function.name: bash_exec
function.description: Execute a bash shell command within the project workspace. Use when: (1) running builds or automated tests, (2) checking system processes, or (3) inspecting git history. Do NOT use bash_exec to write/edit files (use file_write or file_edit instead). Do NOT use bash_exec to dispatch slash commands (use slash_command_exec instead). Examples: command="cargo test", command="./tests/test_cron.sh", command="git status".

command.description: The bash shell command string to execute (e.g. "cargo build", "git status").

function.name: file_read
function.description: Read a targeted range of lines from a local file in the workspace or semantic memory (auto-paginated, default: 100 lines, max: 200). Supports reading working memory with path="mem:active_task". Use when: inspecting source code, reading configs before modifying them, or inspecting task deliverables. Examples: path="lib/cron.sh", start_line=1, max_lines=100; path="mem:active_task", start_line=1, max_lines=100.

path.description: Relative file path from workspace root (e.g. "lib/cron.sh", "web/src/main.rs") or semantic memory handle ("mem:active_task").

max_lines.description: Number of lines to read (default: 100, max: 200). Inspect code in 100-200 line chunks.

function.name: pdf_read
function.description: Extract text and structured page content from a PDF document using Poppler pdftotext. Use when: inspecting specification PDFs, research papers, or documentation. Examples: path="docs/spec.pdf", max_pages=10.

path.description: Relative file path from workspace root or absolute path to the PDF.

max_pages.description: Optional maximum number of pages to extract (default: 20).

layout.description: Preserve visual column and tabular layout (default: true).

function.name: workflow_plan
function.description: Initiate interactive feature/task planning with George and the operator. Clarifies requirements, formulates implementation scope, asks critical design questions, and drafts an implementation plan contract before editing code or running deep tasks. Use when: approaching multi-component features or breaking changes. Examples: objective="Implement distributed telemetry worker", questions="Should we use MQTT or WebSockets?".

objective.description: Primary goal, feature requirement, or research objective to plan.

context.description: Optional background information, constraints, or findings to consider.

questions.description: Optional clarifying questions or design tradeoffs for George and the operator to answer.

function.name: workflow_run
function.description: Execute a Blue Lodge multi-agent workflow to perform coordinated team operations. Use when: delegating complete lifecycle phases (planning, audit, verification). Examples: name="the-architect", args="design metrics service"; name="tester", args="run all cron tests".

name.description: Name of the workflow to run (e.g. the-architect, dispatcher, george, tester, etc.).

args.description: Arguments, context, or task description passed to the workflow.

function.name: task_wait
function.description: Suspend execution and sleep for N seconds (e.g. waiting for a background service, test completion, or timeout). Returns cleanly when the timer expires. Examples: seconds=5, reason="Wait for background service startup"; seconds=15, reason="Wait for build completion".

seconds.description: Number of seconds to wait (1 to 600).

reason.description: Explanation of what is being waited on.

function.name: tool_search
function.description: Search the sovereign tool catalog using natural language intent or category tags (e.g. +ops, +git, +social, +web, cron scheduling, docker). Dynamically auto-mounts discovered tools into your active session. Use when: you need a capability not in your current profile or are unsure how to perform an action. Examples: query="how to schedule recurring task", query="+ops", query="docker container exec".

query.description: The search query, task intent, or bundle name (e.g. "+ops", "how to schedule cron", "+git").

function.name: task_complete
function.description: Signal that the overall task or user objective is completely fulfilled. Submits the final output deliverable to the Outer Loop Evaluator for final determination. Use when: you have completed all objectives, tested execution, and are delivering the final response. Examples: summary="The meme report cron job issue has been resolved and verified with a live test run.", artifacts=[".george/cron_jobs/meme_report.sh"].

summary.description: The complete final response, synthesis, or deliverable report for the operator.

artifacts.description: Optional list of modified or created file paths.

function.name: milestone_complete
function.description: Signal that an intermediate milestone is complete or blocked, and submit structured observations and discovered facts to the DAG state barrier. Use when: you have fulfilled an intermediate milestone task and need to advance to the next step. Do NOT call milestone_complete on the final synthesis/reply step — simply write your final response directly as plain text to complete the task. Examples: status="success", summary="Phytology status verified: 66 Cambium modules operational.", facts_discovered=["Cambium kernel healthy", "0 syntax errors"]; status="blocked", summary="Missing required dependency cargo-tarpaulin".

status.description: Whether the milestone was successfully completed or is blocked.

summary.description: Concise summary of actions taken, discoveries made, or blocking reasons.

facts_discovered.description: Key factual findings or artifacts produced during this milestone.

function.name: file_write
function.description:
Create a new file or completely overwrite an existing file with specified content. Use when: (1) creating new scripts in .george/tools/ or .george/cron_jobs/, (2) creating new microservice source files, (3) writing complete new modules, or (4) saving persistent task deliverables, research summaries, and working notes using path="mem:active_task". Do NOT use for small surgical edits to large files (use file_edit instead). Examples: path=".george/cron_jobs/cache_cleaner.sh", content="#!/bin/bash
# INTERVAL: 3600
# DESC: Purges cache
rm -rf /tmp/cache/*
"; path="mem:active_task", content="# Task Report
Synthesized findings here.
".

path.description: Relative file path from workspace root (e.g. ".george/cron_jobs/my_job.sh") or semantic memory handle ("mem:active_task").

content.description: Full text content to write to the file.

function.name: file_append
function.description:
Append text content to the end of an existing file or active memory scratchpad. Use when: adding log entries, appending new exports, or writing sequentially to memory files (path="mem:active_task"). Examples: path="GEORGE.md", content="
- Custom note"; path="mem:active_task", content="
## Step 2 Findings
Details...".

path.description: Relative file path or semantic memory handle ("mem:active_task").

function.name: file_edit
function.description:
Edit an existing file in place. Two forms for `expression`: (1) a SINGLE-LINE sed substitution such as s/let port = 8080;/let port = 3000;/g (no newlines in the pattern); (2) for multi-line changes, one or more blocks:
<<<<<<< SEARCH
exact existing lines
=======
replacement lines
>>>>>>> REPLACE
SEARCH text must match the file exactly (no line numbers). If the edit cannot be applied the file is left unchanged and an ERROR is returned. Edits that break shell syntax (bash -n) are reverted.

path.description: Target file path relative to workspace root (e.g. "GEORGE.md", "web/src/main.rs").

expression.description: Single-line sed s/old/new/[g] OR SEARCH/REPLACE block(s) for multi-line edits.

function.name: crypto_plan
function.description: Propose trading actions WITHOUT executing them. Returns plan_id (P-XXXXXX), each action with price, model fill probability, fees, EV where a fair value exists, permission tier and the policy checks it passed or failed, plus how_to_execute. Plans expire after 10 minutes or if price moves > 0.5 sigma. Intents: 'review' (re-evaluate open orders and inventory: reprices, exits, reclaims), 'exit SNEK', 'buy NIGHT 60' (ADA budget; optional '@ 0.19' price), 'reclaim <order_id>', 'move <order_id> to NIGHT', 'unlock S2_shock_fade', or JSON like {"kind":"buy","asset":"NIGHT","budget_ada":60,"strategy":"manual"}. Tier A plans you may execute yourself and report after; Tier B plans need the operator to reply 'confirm <plan_id>': tell them the plan_id and what it does, then stop. Never call crypto_execute without a plan_id returned by crypto_plan.

intent.description: Intent phrase or JSON object (see description). Default 'review'.

function.name: crypto_execute
function.description: Execute a plan from crypto_plan. Re-checks freshness, capital rules and tiers against live chain state. Tier A runs; Tier B is refused unless the operator confirmed it (their 'confirm <plan_id>' reply executes it automatically, so you normally never need to call this for Tier B). Strategies in 'simulated' state are journalled, not traded. Report every result to the operator. Never call crypto_execute without a plan_id returned by crypto_plan.

confirm_token.description: Only if the operator's confirmation flow handed you one. Never invent it.

function.name: sdr_query
function.description: Query and filter the Sovereign P25 SDR Radio Lab SQLite database (sdr_intel.db) by time window (hours), talkgroup ID or department/agency name (e.g. 'Metro PD', 'County EMS', 'City Fire', 'County Sheriff', '61591'), radio unit ID (e.g. '7100001'), category (LAW_ENFORCEMENT, FIRE_RESCUE, EMS, PUBLIC_WORKS), or keyword/street search. Returns summary statistics, active talkgroups, cross-channel unit timelines, ongoing department narratives, and transcripts with local .m4a file paths.

hours.description: Lookback window in hours (default 24.0 for full day; use 3.0 for 3-hour window, 168.0 for 7 days).

talkgroup.description: Optional talkgroup filter: numeric TGID (e.g. '61591', '61615') or department/tag substring (e.g. 'Metro PD', 'County EMS', 'Springfield', 'County', 'County', 'Fire').

unit_id.description: Optional P25 radio unit ID filter (e.g. '7100001', '7191333', '4589316') to trace a specific squad, medic, or dispatch console across channels.

category.description: Optional category filter: LAW_ENFORCEMENT, FIRE_RESCUE, EMS, PUBLIC_WORKS, or PUBLIC_SAFETY.

search.description: Optional keyword, ten-code, incident type, or street/location search across transcripts and tactical summaries.

emergency_only.description: If true, return only emergency or priority radio transmissions.

mode.description: Output focus mode: 'summary' (stats + narrative + calls), 'stats' (aggregate database & talkgroup statistics), 'calls' (detailed transcripts), or 'unit_timeline' (chronological unit tracking).

limit.description: Maximum number of individual call records to include (default 40, max 200).

function.name: sdr_listen
function.description: Consume an SDR P25 radio .m4a or .wav recording (by call_id, 'latest', or file path) into the Two-Stage Audio Encoder Pipeline (FFmpeg 260-3400Hz bandpass + Whisper P25-A100-LoRA ASR + Gemma-4 E4B Multimodal audio encoder with Running Context Buffer). Returns the refined transcript, acoustic draft, tactical summary, custom question answer, and local .m4a file path (which can be uploaded to Discord via discord_send_file).

call_id.description: The SDR call_id (e.g. '61615-1792340748.780_857737500.0-call_7'), 'latest' for the newest intelligible call, or a direct local .m4a/.wav file path.

prompt.description: Optional specific question or analysis instruction for the Gemma-4 E4B audio encoder while listening to the recording (e.g. 'What street name or unit number was said?', 'Verify if 10-4 was spoken', 'Describe background sounds and urgency').
